odc.short: The S-shaped curve of haemoglobin saturation against PO₂. Flat at the top (loading in the lungs is safe), steep in the middle (unloading in tissues is easy).

p50.short: The PO₂ at which haemoglobin is 50% saturated: about 26–27 mmHg in normal blood at pH 7.4 and 37 °C. Higher P50 = lower affinity = curve shifted right.

bohr-effect.short: Lower affinity of haemoglobin for O₂ when acidity (H⁺) and CO₂ rise, which shifts the curve right and helps unload O₂ in working muscle.

dpg.short: A by-product of red-cell glycolysis that binds deoxyhaemoglobin and shifts the curve right. It changes over days (altitude, training), not within one session.

sao2.short: The share of haemoglobin binding sites in arterial blood that carry O₂, as a %. About 97–98% at rest at sea level. SpO₂ is the same thing estimated by a pulse oximeter.

cao2.short: How much O₂ a volume of arterial blood carries, bound plus dissolved: about 200 mL·L⁻¹ (20 mL·dL⁻¹) in a healthy person at sea level.

fick-principle.short: O₂ uptake = blood flow × the O₂ the blood gives up on the way through: V̇O₂ = Q̇ × (CaO₂ − CvO₂). Works for the whole body or one muscle.

o2-extraction.short: The share of the O₂ arriving in arterial blood that the tissue takes out: a-vO₂ difference ÷ CaO₂. About 25% for the whole body at rest, about 90% at VO₂max in trained people.

co-rebreathing.short: The standard way to measure total haemoglobin mass: breathe a small known dose of carbon monoxide for about 2 min and measure how much the blood's carboxyhaemoglobin rises.

plasma-volume.short: The volume of the fluid part of blood. It shrinks during hard exercise (concentrating everything in it) and expands with endurance training.

myoglobin.short: An O₂-binding protein inside oxidative muscle fibres (and heart). It holds O₂ much more tightly than haemoglobin (P50 about 3 mmHg) and helps O₂ diffuse to the mitochondria.

transit-time.short: How long a red cell spends in a capillary: capillary blood volume ÷ blood flow. Longer time gives more chance to unload O₂.

hb-affinity.short: How tightly haemoglobin holds on to O₂. High affinity: it grabs O₂ easily but lets go reluctantly. Low affinity: it lets go easily. Measured by P50.

mixed-venous-blood.short: The blood returning from the whole body, mixed together in the right side of the heart and the pulmonary artery. Its O₂ content shows how much O₂ the body as a whole left unused.

epo.short: A hormone made by the kidneys that tells the bone marrow to make more red cells. It rises at altitude; taken as a drug, it is doping.
